title: Divine Assistance in Worship
summary: Divine assistance in worship is a blessing; seek, express gratitude, and reflect on actions.
translation:
Receiving even the slightest opportunity for worship from Allah is a blessing from Him. Many, despite their desire, cannot worship. It might be due to personal leniency or unavoidable circumstances preventing them from continually doing the worship they wish. Ultimately, this is subject to Allah’s will; He may withhold from some and bestow His mercy on others. Therefore, when granted the ability to worship, whether it’s to cry, pray, fast, or perform salah, one should be grateful to Allah and seek further blessings, asking for consistency in these acts.

Hazrat Muhammad bin Abu Humaira رضی اللہ تعالیٰ عنہ, a companion of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وسلم, said that if a person were to worship Allah from birth until death, dedicating their entire life to it, even then, on the Day of Judgment, in seeing the reward for their deeds, they would consider their efforts too little. They would wish to return to the world to perform more good deeds, increasing their reward. It's clear that a long life coupled with the ability to worship is a great bounty, provided it is not wasted but spent in obedience, worship, service to the religion, and good deeds. The longer the life and the more opportunities for good deeds, the greater the reward will be, serving as the greatest asset on the Day of Judgment.

One should therefore pray to Allah and express gratitude for the ability to worship. If one lacks this opportunity, consider it a sign of Allah's displeasure. Reflect on any actions that may have provoked this and seek forgiveness. Repent and strive to reconnect with Allah, who will then restore His blessings.
